answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A falcon delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A saffron check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A ember penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 4944 identities need 4944 bonds of 33 tokens, 18980 dollars of hardware and 23 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
